question: Should Browser CLI `--fields-file` begin rejecting existing valid JSON inputs above 1 MiB, and if so what established Browser or Gateway contract defines that threshold and upgrade behavior?
rationale: The code and docs can implement a chosen limit, but only maintainers can decide whether the new rejection is an acceptable public CLI compatibility change and whether another existing payload boundary should govern it.

options.title: Preserve existing compatibility
options.body: Do not add a new 1 MiB rejection unless the Browser CLI already has a documented compatible size contract.

options.title: Approve a documented 1 MiB limit
options.body: Treat 1 MiB as a deliberate public Browser CLI contract and add explicit upgrade rationale and compatibility coverage before merge.

options.title: Use an existing payload boundary
options.body: Align validation with the applicable Browser or Gateway request-size contract instead of creating a separate fields-file-only cap.

recommendation.title: Preserve existing compatibility
recommendation.body: Do not add a new 1 MiB rejection unless the Browser CLI already has a documented compatible size contract.
